Definition: some kind of nuttree, perhaps the almond
BiblicalUsage: The word names a kind of nut tree, probably the almond or hazel, and it appears once, when Jacob took rods of green poplar, hazel and chestnut and peeled white streaks in them. The rods were part of his bargain with Laban over the flocks.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that God worked through Jacob's ordinary tools, and the rods remind me He blesses the work of our hands without needing our schemes.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
